blocks.label: Reverse Nodes in k-Group (LC25)
blocks.py:
def reverse_k_group(head, k):
    check, cnt = head, 0
    while check and cnt < k: check = check.next; cnt += 1
    if cnt < k: return head          # partial tail untouched

    prev, cur = None, head
    for _ in range(k):               # reverse exactly this group
        ahead = cur.next; cur.next = prev
        prev, cur = cur, ahead
    head.next = reverse_k_group(cur, k)   # MANTRA: rest recursive
    return prev

blocks.label: Merge-k preview (LC23) — heap of heads
blocks.py:
import heapq
heap = [(l.val, i, l) for i, l in enumerate(lists) if l]
heapq.heapify(heap)                   # (val, tiebreak, node) triples
dummy = Node(0); tail = dummy
while heap:
    v, i, node = heapq.heappop(heap)
    tail.next = node; tail = tail.next
    if node.next: heapq.heappush(heap, (node.next.val, i, node.next))
return dummy.next                     # N log k accounting

chain.q: Why does rotate-list use mod before walking?
chain.a: k>n wraps fully; k%n hops with end-connector trick: make list circular, advance n−(k%n), break.
Reversals in-place O(1); avoid new/delete inside loops when reuse possible; mention RAII/smart-pointer ownership from Foundations L3 if interviewer pushes lifetime safety.

chain.q: When is std::list actually right in production?
chain.a: Heavy splicing/merging of large elements with stable iterators — O(1) splice is unique; otherwise vector wins cache wars (recall Foundations L3 layout stories).
